title: Video remix
summary: Remix an authorised source clip with approved character, object or style references: local substitution, motion transfer or restyling through an immutable Genjutsu preparation.

en: replace a person in a video

notFor.when: a new film generated shot by shot without a source performance
tightening a recorded talk or adding its subtitles
borrowing a reference film's craft for a new product story

qa: The correct mode follows the requested operation
All markers resolve to their exact one-based attachments
Originals, selected segment, entity revisions and prompt match the approved preparation
Input review, source-use rights and generation budget are current
The exact result has a recorded comparison review; a reshoot requires the user's decision
Source music and likeness permissions are separate from a clip's popularity

intake.ask: Which element changes, and what must remain unchanged?
intake.why: Selects object-swap, motion-transfer or restyle and identifies the target

intake.ask: Do you have an authorised source clip and approved identity references?
intake.why: Missing originals are sourced or prepared before generation; a preview is not an original

intake.ask: Which segment, crop, audio policy, placements and generation budget are authorised?
intake.why: Pins the measured input, source-use permissions and paid attempt bounds

variants.title: Local replacement
variants.changes: Describe the selected target unambiguously; preserve the other subjects, environment, action and camera. A face-only replacement preserves the source outfit unless explicitly changed.

variants.title: Rebuild around motion
variants.changes: Use source movement and camera as the performance; specify the new characters and scene from approved references. Do not promise that the old background remains intact.

variants.title: Visual restyling
variants.changes: Use a current preset UUID; optional character references; retain composition and motion, and inspect any changed cadence and audio.
